exam_format: Computer-based, fixed-form (not adaptive); at Prometric test centers only — no at-home option. Four sections with optional scheduled breaks between each section. Total seated time approximately 7 hours 30 minutes (includes tutorial, void option, breaks). Section order is fixed: CPBS, CARS, BBFL, PSBF. Void option: candidate may void all scores at the end of the exam at no cost; voided scores are not reported.
exam_price_notes: $335 USD standard registration; $375 USD late registration. Fee assistance program (FAP) available for eligible applicants: reduces fee to $135. Rescheduling and cancellation fees apply; see aamc.org for current fee schedule.

testing_centers.notes: MCAT is available exclusively at Prometric test centers. No at-home or online proctored option is available. Register via the AAMC registration portal at students-residents.aamc.org. Seats are limited; register early, especially for spring testing dates (most competitive). Test centers are located throughout the United States, Canada, and select international locations.

id_requirements: One government-issued, unexpired photo ID required (e.g., driver's license, passport). Name on ID must exactly match name on AAMC registration. A second acceptable form of ID is recommended as backup. Biometric data (fingerprint or palm vein scan) collected at some Prometric centers.
exam_rules: No personal items permitted in the testing room. Scratch paper (laminated noteboard and marker) provided at the test center — no outside materials. No unauthorized electronic devices, notes, food, or drinks in the testing room (small snack/drink for break consumption only, stored in locker). Bathroom breaks permitted between sections only (breaks are scheduled). Candidates may opt to void all scores at the end of the exam; once voided, scores cannot be recovered. Attempting to access testing materials or communicate with others during the exam may result in score cancellation and a ban from future MCAT administrations.
renewal_options: MCAT scores are not certifications requiring renewal. Most medical schools accept MCAT scores up to 3 years old at the time of matriculation; some schools accept scores up to 2 years old, and some up to 5 years old. Verify score acceptance windows directly with each medical school. Candidates may retake the MCAT within lifetime attempt limits to obtain higher or more recent scores.

retake_policy.notes: Up to 3 MCAT attempts per testing year (Jan 1–Dec 31). Up to 4 attempts in any 2 consecutive testing years. Maximum 7 lifetime attempts. All non-voided scores are reported to schools (no score selection). Score release is approximately 30-35 days after the test date. Scores from voided exams or no-shows are not reported.

domains.name: Chemical and Physical Foundations of Biological Systems (CPBS): general chemistry, physics, biochemistry, organic chemistry
Critical Analysis and Reasoning Skills (CARS): reading comprehension, inference, argument evaluation
Biological and Biochemical Foundations of Living Systems (BBFL): biology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, general chemistry
Psychological, Social, and Biological Foundations of Behavior (PSBF): psychology, sociology, biology

editorial.meta_description: The MCAT is a computer-based exam that evaluates candidates on the chemical, physical, biological, and psychological foundations of systems and reasoning.
editorial.overview: The Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) is a computer-based exam that evaluates candidates across four distinct domains: chemical and physical foundations, critical analysis and reasoning, biological and biochemical foundations, and psychological, social, and biological foundations of behavior. Each of the four sections carries a weight of 25 percent, providing a balanced assessment of the knowledge and skills required for medical school. This evaluation ensures that all prospective students demonstrate the necessary proficiency in scientific inquiry and critical thinking before entering their medical education programs.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for individuals applying to medical school. Candidates must be prepared for a 450-minute testing session that includes 230 questions. It is a fixed-form, computer-based assessment administered exclusively at Prometric test centers, requiring preparation to succeed in this academic environment.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official AAMC exam objectives to understand the scope of the four sections. Practice with passage-based and discrete questions to build familiarity with the fixed-form, computer-based format. Manage your time effectively during the 450-minute exam. Utilize the fee assistance program if eligible to reduce the standard registration cost of $335 to $135. Consistent practice and a deep understanding of the core scientific principles are required for achieving a competitive score on this assessment.

domain_guidance.summary: This section covers the chemical and physical principles that govern biological systems. It requires knowledge of general chemistry, physics, biochemistry, and organic chemistry to solve problems related to biological functions and systems.

This domain tests your ability to comprehend, analyze, and evaluate complex passages. It focuses on reading comprehension, logical inference, and the evaluation of arguments presented in written text to determine your analytical capabilities.

This section examines biological and biochemical processes in living systems. It integrates concepts from biology, biochemistry, organic chemistry, and general chemistry to explain life at the molecular and cellular levels for medical students.

This domain addresses the psychological, social, and biological foundations of behavior. It covers concepts from psychology and sociology as they relate to human biology and behavior to assess your understanding of complex social systems.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at your assigned Prometric test center for the computer-based exam. The test consists of four fixed-order sections with optional scheduled breaks. You may choose to void your scores at the end of the session if you feel your performance was not representative.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam consists of 230 questions distributed across four sections. Each section contributes equally to the total, with each domain representing 25 percent of the content to ensure a balanced and fair assessment of all candidates.

The AAMC does not define a specific passing score for the MCAT. Candidates should check with AAMC or their target medical schools for information regarding score requirements and the current certification path for their specific application goals.

The total duration of the exam is 450 minutes. This includes the time for the four sections, the tutorial, the void option, and the optional scheduled breaks between sections to allow for rest and mental preparation during the day.

faq.question_title: What is the cost to register for the exam?
faq.answer_text: Standard registration is $335, while late registration is $375. Eligible applicants may use the fee assistance program to reduce the cost to $135. Rescheduling and cancellation fees also apply, so please review the official policy carefully before finalizing your registration.

methodology.summary: This page was built by synthesizing verified facts provided by the AAMC and official exam documentation to ensure accuracy regarding the current testing requirements, structure, and administrative policies for all prospective medical school applicants.
